doc: Help cards. methods: stamped (and queued) method name → card. combos: <board>/<head>/<family> using site ids (main=Full genome, dev=Chromosome 21, entrants=2019 challenge; count_arm is the Count-head distributional family). Every fact is from the 2026-08-27 dossier or from registry/boards/rows. Where the dossier says UNKNOWN/UNVERIFIED, this file says not recorded. metrics: <arm>/<key> (diagnostics/<key> when arm is null) → question, formula_mathml, estimator_notes, read_rules. Formulas are MathML of what this repo computes. Where a fact is not recorded, the card says not recorded.

eDICE.what: A per-bin attention imputer (PyTorch reimplementation of Hawkins-Hooker et al. 2023): one ~6 million-parameter model with no positional parameters, so one set of weights predicts any genomic position. Retrained by us on Dataset-2 EIC — not the 2019 submission.
eDICE.training: Retrained by us on the EIC store, regime eic_val. 51 training cells, 267 p-value tracks, 35 assays. Train chromosomes: chromosome 19 only. Seed 211, paper defaults, 50 epochs. Target is arcsinh(−log10 p), MSE loss. Masks 31 of 267 tracks per bin (the paper’s 11.6% rate). No validation or blind-test track in the model’s training or support. σ-fit is a scoring step, not training: it uses validation-pair residuals (see How it is scored).
eDICE.classes: Position-generalizing (no genomic-position parameters; Full genome is still held-out sequence because training used chromosome-19 bins only). Retrained per setting: a validation cell has no learned embedding; prediction uses the paired training-cell embedding. That is same-cell-type transduction, not an unseen cell type.
eDICE.scoring: External predictions scored by candi.bench.external. σ-table fitted on validation-pair residuals, chromosome 21 only, and reused unchanged on the full genome. PIT KS and 95% coverage on this row describe that wrap, not a forecast eDICE emitted. No peak head: peak AUPRC is a coverage ranking from the predicted signal. No count arm.
caveats: Masks 31 of 267 tracks per bin, not a fixed 120.
Uses the paired training-cell embedding for the validation cell.
Predicted signal is clipped at 0.
Validation-pair CRPS is in-sample for the fitted spread.
No count head and no peak head.

ChromImpute.what: Jason Ernst’s published Java imputer (jar v1.0.5): an ensemble of regression trees over neighbouring samples and local windows. Retrained by us with paper defaults; we convert store tracks in and out — the jar does the modelling.
ChromImpute.training: Retrained by us on the EIC store, regime eic_val. 267 training tracks, 51 training cells, 35 marks. Trained genome-wide once, then scored as chromosome 21 and as the full genome. Apply target is (training cell, missing mark); truth is that mark on the paired validation cell.
ChromImpute.classes: Position-transductive: trees train at positions where the target mark was observed in other training samples, including the evaluation chromosome. On Full genome the method is in-sample at every position, including the chromosome-19-removed view. Retrained per setting: one ensemble per (training cell, mark); not zero-shot on a new cell type.
ChromImpute.scoring: External predictions scored by candi.bench.external. σ-table fitted on chromosome-21 validation-pair residuals in −log10 p and reused on the full genome. Peak AUPRC is a coverage ranking. Predictions are quantized to 0.01 by the jar. No count arm.
caveats: Position-transductive everywhere, including the chromosome-19-removed view.
Validation-pair CRPS is in-sample for σ; σ fitted on chromosome 21 and applied genome-wide, where mean squared error is about 32% higher.
The fitted Gaussian is heavy-tailed / miscalibrated (95% coverage ~0.98, PIT KS ~0.37).
No count arm.
Pilot chromosome-21-only numbers are not results.

Avocado.what: Tensor factorisation over (cell, assay, position): one MLP on concatenated cell, assay, and per-position genomic factors (Schreiber, Bilmes & Noble 2020). Max’s PyTorch port, vendored byte-identical, retrained by us. Cannot predict a position it never fitted.
Avocado.training: Retrained by us on the EIC store, regime eic_val, 267 training-split columns (51 cells × 35 assays). Seed 0. Target arcsinh(−log10 p). 60-epoch joint fit on chromosome 20, then 30-epoch per-chromosome genomic factors with shared weights frozen — all 23 store chromosomes. Last epoch, not best-on-held-out. Training and validation cells of the same type share one cell index; the embedding is learned only from training-cell tracks.
Avocado.classes: Position-transductive. Full genome is in-sample sequence on every chromosome, including the chromosome-19-removed view. Cell embedding exists for eval cell types via the paired training tracks, not via a never-seen cell type. Retrained per setting.
Avocado.scoring: External predictions scored by candi.bench.external. σ-table fitted on chromosome-21 validation-pair residuals and reused on a full-genome score that exists but is not stamped. Peak AUPRC is a coverage ranking. No count arm. Stamped only on Chromosome 21. No Full-genome row is stamped; Full-genome pending does not list Avocado.
caveats: This retrain is separate from the frozen 2019 Avocado_p0 tracks.
Full genome structurally favours this method versus chromosome-19-only CANDI.
The fitted-spread miscalibration (PIT KS ~0.37, 95% coverage ~0.98) is a property of the wrap, not of Avocado’s point predictions.
Validation-pair CRPS is in-sample for σ.
AUPRC is a coverage ranking; quote it with the peak base rate.
Why the full-genome score was not stamped is not recorded.
Architecture is not recorded in this tree.

avg.what: Leave-one-out cross-cell average: the EIC Average definition on Dataset-2, built by us from training biosamples only (not the 2019 Average bigwigs).
avg.training: Not a trained model. Contributors are training biosamples that carry the assay, minus any cell sharing the input’s or target’s cell-type suffix. P-value: plain mean of −log10 p. Spread: cross-cell standard deviation. Counts: moment-matched negative binomial after depth-rescaling to the target. Peak: fraction of contributors with a store peak at the bin. Poisson floor on the stamped row is n=1e4, not the pre-registered 1e6. Train chromosomes do not enter the average itself; exclusion is over cells.
avg.classes: Position-generalizing, zero-shot cell types (no positional parameters and no learned cell embedding). On Full genome, neighbour methods that use chromosome 19 would be in-sample there; avg’s exclusion is over cells, not positions. Still zero-shot only in the “no cell embedding” sense: this round is not a fully-unseen-cell-type split.
avg.scoring: External scorer. Native heteroscedastic spread (no σ-table). Native peak score, so this is a peak head, not a coverage ranking. Count arm present. Stamped only on Chromosome 21. Full genome lists avg as still computing. Whether full-genome count-arm scoring finished after 2026-08-26 is not recorded.
caveats: Distinct from the 2019 Average submission. The table names differ by a capital A and three letters; 2019 Average uses train+validation contributors, this avg uses train-only.
Count CRPS used n=1e4 floor, not 1e6.
Native spread, not the rival common-mode wrap — calibration on chromosome 21 (PIT KS 0.336, 95% coverage 0.888) is not the rival common-mode.
Beats the marginal baseline on 38 of 45 tracks; that is an accepted finding.
Some count-scale companion numbers are unreliable at this floor.

knn5.what: k-nearest-neighbour average, k=5: same heads as avg, but only over the five training cells most similar to the input cell.
knn5.training: Same contributor pool and exclusion as avg. Similarity: mean Pearson correlation over assays both cells carry, on train chromosomes only (chromosome 19), in arcsinh(−log10 p) — cell-level, not per-assay. Same n=1e4 count floor. EIC store, regime eic_val.
knn5.classes: Position-generalizing, zero-shot cell types (no learned cell embedding — not a cell type with no training experiment). On Full genome the similarity table, and therefore neighbour choice, is in-sample on chromosome 19. This round is not a fully-unseen-cell-type split.
knn5.scoring: Same as avg: native spread and native peak score, no σ-table. Stamped on Chromosome 21 only; Full genome lists knn5 as still computing.
caveats: Same floor and sampling notes as avg.
On chromosome 21, p-value CRPS 0.3240 vs avg 0.3237 is not a significant gap.

knn1.what: BestSingle: copy the single most similar training cell (same similarity table as knn5).
knn1.training: Same pool, exclusion, and similarity as knn5; k=1. P-value: that cell’s −log10 p (no spread). Counts: that cell, Poisson floor. Peak: that cell’s peak calls. n=1e4 floor on the stamped count arm.
knn1.classes: Position-generalizing, zero-shot cell types (no learned cell embedding — not a cell type with no training experiment). Same chromosome-19 in-sample note for similarity as knn5. This round is not a fully-unseen-cell-type split.
knn1.scoring: External scorer; no σ-table. No p-value CRPS, PIT KS, 95% coverage, or Gaussian NLL — there is no p-value distribution. Peak is native (copied calls). Count arm present. Stamped on Chromosome 21 only; not listed as pending on Full genome.
caveats: No cross-cell spread, so no p-value CRPS. One contributor.

avg-arcsinh.what: Variant of the cross-cell average: the mean is taken in arcsinh space, then sinh back. Not the EIC Average.
avg-arcsinh.training: Same contributors as avg. Emits a point p-value track only — no spread, no counts, no peak score.
avg-arcsinh.classes: Position-generalizing, zero-shot cell types (no learned cell embedding — not a cell type with no training experiment). This round is not a fully-unseen-cell-type split.
avg-arcsinh.scoring: External scorer, no σ-table. Missing count arm and p-value distributional/loss keys. Peak AUPRC is a coverage ranking from the predicted signal. Stamped on Chromosome 21. A full-genome score exists but no Full-genome row is stamped, and it is not listed as pending.
caveats: Never present as the EIC baseline.
Down-weights tall bins.

marginal.what: Weakest distributional baseline: one constant Gaussian and one constant negative binomial per assay, fitted on training cells × train chromosomes, scaled to the target track’s depth. No per-bin ranking.
marginal.training: Moment match over all bins of training cells’ tracks on train chromosomes only (chromosome 19), then depth-scale to the target. No peak score. EIC store, regime eic_val.
marginal.classes: Position-generalizing, zero-shot cell types (no learned cell embedding — not a cell type with no training experiment). On Full genome the constants are in-sample on chromosome 19. This round is not a fully-unseen-cell-type split.
marginal.scoring: Native constant spread (no σ-table). Count arm present. Genome-wide Pearson and Spearman are missing — a constant has no rank correlation. AUPRC equals the peak base rate (0.01375 on chromosome 21): coverage ranking of a constant, which is the chance line. Stamped on Chromosome 21 only.
caveats: No peak head.
P-value CRPS 1.691 with PIT KS 0.450 and 95% coverage 0.993 — a different calibration failure from the rival wrap.
On Full genome, in-sample on chromosome 19 for the fitted constants.

Lavawizard.what: Two different rows share this name. Dataset-2: a planned retrain of the 2019 Guacamole/Lavawizard architecture (Avocado-style tensor factorisation plus a cross-cell average skip). That retrain is not done. 2019: the frozen round-2 submission of the same team (joint second in the challenge). Do not treat the 2019 row as the Dataset-2 retrain.
Lavawizard.training: Dataset-2 training is not recorded — no EIC retrain exists. Planned: EIC store, regime eic_val, same σ-fit rule as other rivals. Upstream weights live on Synapse; they are not in this tree. Whether the average feature may include the target cell, and whether the average is train-only or train+validation, is not recorded as decided. 2019 training is not recorded beyond “2019 challenge training.”
Lavawizard.classes: Not stamped on Full genome or Chromosome 21 (listed with note “Dataset-2 retrain not started”). Architecture would be position-transductive if retrained like Avocado — not recorded until a Dataset-2 row is stamped. The 2019 row has position class unrecorded and cell-type class unrecorded.
Lavawizard.scoring: Dataset-2: planned external scorer plus σ-table; no Dataset-2 score json is in this tree. 2019: same 2019 scorer path as the other frozen submissions, 48 experiments.
caveats: The Dataset-2 port is not gated (parity versus Keras weights was not run).
The competitor directory named in the memo is not in this worktree.
Same team as Guacamole; the two 2019 submissions are not identical tracks.

CANDI.what: The CANDI model: grouped Conv1D plus a DNA tower plus a RoPE transformer, then a grouped decoder with FiLM and a depth-offset negative-binomial count head. The queued runs also train a Gaussian signal head and a Bernoulli peak head. No CANDI row is stamped yet; two runs are training.
CANDI.training: Both queued runs use the store, heads count+signal+peak, offset on, seed 0, weight decay 0, width 288. Chromosome-19 / mainline: regime eic_val, 25 epochs; train on chromosome 19; eval on chromosome 21; 51 training cells, 35 assays, 26 pairs. Genome-wide: regime eic_gw, 4 epochs; train on every store chromosome except chromosome 21. Neither script has been observed to complete here. Job status and checkpoints are not recorded.
CANDI.classes: Not stamped. Intended reading: the chromosome-19 recipe is position-generalizing except that the all-chromosomes view is in-sample on chromosome 19. The genome-wide recipe would be in-sample on 22 of 23 chromosomes — the Main-board in-sample caveat written for chromosome-19-only CANDI would be wrong for that run unless restated. Cell: CANDI conditions on covariates, not a per-cell embedding; this round is still training-to-validation of seen cell types. Position and cell badges are not recorded until stamped.
CANDI.scoring: Internal bench (not the external rival scorer). That path emits a native negative binomial on counts, a native Gaussian on p-values, and a native peak probability. Covariate-sensitivity numbers can only come from this internal path. Count CRPS is closed form unless an approximation flag is set.
caveats: Training count+signal+peak is a different objective from count-only.
Quote count CRPS with its oracle-scaled / scale-error split and the noise floor.
The genome-wide run is 4 epochs versus 25 — not a matched compute comparison with the chromosome-19 run or with Avocado’s 60/30.
Blind-test pairs are not these jobs.
Full genome and Chromosome 21 list CANDI as pending until a row is stamped.

Average.what: Organizer Average baseline, scored from published 2019 bigwigs on the official grid. Frozen 2019 baseline, not our Dataset-2 avg.
Average.training: Round-2 “training set” = train + validation, not train alone (ATAC has no validation experiments; train-only fails the published match). 287 contributor tracks over 23 assays from 312 train+val bigwigs. A bit-identical gate versus the original scorer matched 510 rows × 8 measures at relative difference 0.0.
Average.classes: Position-generalizing, zero-shot cell types (no learned cell embedding). This is the 2019 organizer Average, not Dataset-2 avg.
Average.scoring: Same 2019 scorer path as the other frozen submissions; 48 experiments after dropping DNase-seq.
caveats: Do not mix with Dataset-2 avg. The table names differ by a capital A and three letters; the contributor sets differ (2019 Average is train+validation; Dataset-2 avg is train-only).
Competitive with most submissions under the challenge recipe.
Architecture is not recorded in this tree.

BrokenNodes.scoring: Vendored 2019 scorer on the official grid (chromosome 1–22 and X). DNase-seq is not scored: 3 of 51 experiments dropped, 48 remain. pval/mse.question: On average, how far is the predicted track from the truth, bin by bin, in squared units?
pval/mse.estimator_notes: Mean squared error on the concatenation of scored chromosomes (eic.dict_to_arr). No ddof. No transform. Track wrap is eic.py::mse; board number is the unweighted mean over tracks (harness.py::macro_mean). 2019 uses the same letters on a different signal, with a different macro recipe (bootstrap mean within experiment; median within assay; mean over assay medians). Computed from eic.py::mse.
pval/mse.read_rules: Lower is better; ranked; no floor. P-value space (pred_space: −log10 p). 2019 uses the same letters on a different signal — never place cells next to Dataset-2. MSE scales with mark range.

pval/gwcorr.question: Do predicted and true values rise and fall together in a straight line, over the whole scored genome?
pval/gwcorr.estimator_notes: Pearson r = np.corrcoef(y, ŷ)[0, 1] on concatenated chromosomes. A constant input returns NaN (eic.py::gwcorr). Correlation is scale-invariant (ddof cancels). Computed from eic.py::gwcorr.
pval/gwcorr.read_rules: Higher is better; ranked; no floor. A constant forecast (marginal) is absent, not zero. 2019 vs Dataset-2: different truth — never translate.

pval/gwspear.question: Do predicted and true values share the same rank order over the scored genome?
pval/gwspear.estimator_notes: ρ = scipy.stats.spearmanr(y, ŷ)[0] (eic.py::gwspear). Scipy default: average ranks on ties. Concatenated chromosomes. Computed from eic.py::gwspear.
pval/gwspear.read_rules: Higher is better; ranked; no floor. Do not quote Pearson and Spearman as a pair across spaces. Same 2019 / Dataset-2 warning: different truth — never translate.

pval/mse1obs.question: On the tallest 1% of observed bins, how far is the prediction?
pval/mse1obs.estimator_notes: N = |y|, n = int(N * 0.01), τ = np.sort(y)[-n] (so N < 100 selects the minimum and thus the whole array). Mask y_i ≥ τ (ties admit more than 1%). Then MSE on the mask. Top-1% is over the concatenation of all scored chromosomes, not per chromosome. Computed from eic.py::mse1obs and _top1_mask.
pval/mse1obs.read_rules: Lower is better; ranked; no floor. The chromosome set is part of the number. 2019 vs Dataset-2: different truth — never translate.

pval/crps.question: If each bin is a Gaussian forecast in −log10 p, how far is that whole distribution from the observed value — not just the centre?
pval/crps.estimator_notes: Per bin, Gneiting–Raftery 2007 closed form (distributional.py::gauss_crps): z = (y − μ) / σ with σ ← max(σ, 10⁻¹²). Track score = mean over bins; board = unweighted mean over tracks. No oracle-scaled split on this arm. Closed form only — no sampled Gaussian CRPS in this code. Rivals: σ is one constant per assay from the fitted table, not per-bin. CANDI store path: μ, σ are the delta-method pushforward of the training-space Gaussian when signal_target_transform ≠ none (invert_signal_prediction). Computed from distributional.py::gauss_crps / gauss_suite.
pval/crps.read_rules: Lower is better; ranked but ordering-only. Always show PIT KS and Coverage 95 beside it. No single noise floor (t57 per-method paired CIs; ties not greyed yet). Rival wrap CRPS is in-sample for σ on chromosome 21. Never quote as a calibrated absolute. Point-only rivals get one Gaussian spread per assay, fitted once on validation-pair residuals (eval chromosome chr21) and reused unchanged. That device is known-miscalibrated (PIT KS 0.367–0.391, 95% coverage 0.977–0.985 on the stamped rival rows). CANDI's per-bin Gaussian signal head does not use this device. Count and p-value CRPS never share a column.

pval/pit_ks.question: If the predicted Gaussians were correct, the observed values’ percentiles would be Uniform(0,1) — how far from uniform are they?
pval/pit_ks.estimator_notes: PIT KS is the Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance of the probability-integral transform from Uniform(0,1). Continuous (non-randomised) PIT u_i = Φ((y_i − μ_i) / σ_i) with σ_i ← max(σ_i, 10⁻¹²). Then PIT-KS = scipy.stats.kstest(u, "uniform").statistic — two-sided D = sup_t |F_n(t) − t|, not a p-value. Discrete PIT (calibration_pit_curve) is not used on this arm. No jitter / randomised PIT. Computed from distributional.py::gauss_suite.
pval/pit_ks.read_rules: Lower is better; companion, never ranked. Always beside p-value CRPS. On rivals this scores the wrap (one σ per assay, fitted on chromosome-21 validation-pair residuals), not a forecast the method emitted. Store-path CANDI: calibration of the delta-method Gaussian, not the head. Known-miscalibrated wrap: PIT KS 0.367–0.391 on the stamped rival rows.

pval/coverage_95.question: What fraction of observed bins fall inside the forecast’s central 95% interval?
pval/coverage_95.estimator_notes: α = 0.025, lo = Φ⁻¹(α; μ, σ), hi = Φ⁻¹(1 − α; μ, σ), coverage = mean(lo ≤ y ≤ hi). σ ← max(σ, 10⁻¹²). Nominal 0.95. This is interval coverage, not ECE. Computed from distributional.py::coverage_gauss, emitted in gauss_suite.
pval/coverage_95.read_rules: No direction; companion, never ranked. Distance from 0.95 is not a sort key. Quote with CRPS + PIT KS. Rival wrap ~0.98 is known miscalibration. On rivals this scores the wrap, not a native forecast.

pval/auprc.question: Ranking bins by the method’s peak score (or, if none, by predicted signal), how well are MACS2 peak bins placed above background?
pval/auprc.estimator_notes: Step-wise average precision, ties collapsed to one threshold (binary.py::average_precision): AP = Σ_k (R_k − R_{k−1}) P_k, with P_k = TP / (TP + FP) and R_k = TP / TP_end. Scores sorted descending (mergesort); equal scores share one threshold (last-of-tie). No positives → NaN. Score vector = peak_score if a peak head exists, else predicted p-value (or count mean). Computed from binary.py::average_precision / binary_suite.
pval/auprc.read_rules: Higher is better; ranked; always quote peak_base_rate. AUROC is not on the board. A point-only rival’s AUPRC is a coverage ranking, not a peak classifier: eDICE, Avocado, and ChromImpute do not output a peak probability, so the scorer ranks each bin by predicted signal against MACS2 labels. CANDI's peak head, when its rows land, emits a per-bin Bernoulli probability and is labeled separately. 2019 has no MACS2 AUPRC (absent, not invented).

pval/peak_base_rate.question: What fraction of scored bins are MACS2 peaks in the validation cell?
pval/peak_base_rate.estimator_notes: peak_base_rate = mean(1[y^peak]) over scored bins (binary.py::binary_suite). Board number is the unweighted mean over tracks.
pval/peak_base_rate.read_rules: Companion, never ranked; no direction. About 0.01375 on chromosome 21, about 0.0169 macro genome-wide. A random ranker’s AUPRC equals this rate. Always quote AUPRC with this number.

pval/gaussian_nll.question: What mean per-bin Gaussian negative log-likelihood does the p-value head (or wrapped Gaussian) assign to held-out truth in the training transform?
pval/gaussian_nll.estimator_notes: full=True Gaussian NLL (distributional.py::gaussian_nll): (1/N) Σ ½(log v_i + (μ_i − y_i)² / v_i + log(2π)), v_i = max(σ_i², 10⁻⁶). Truth is bent forward with transform_signal_target; prediction is not inverted (harness.py::loss_block). External stamped rows: transform none. Future CANDI store path: typically arcsinh — not comparable (D30). Computed from distributional.py::gaussian_nll.
pval/gaussian_nll.read_rules: Lower is better; per_family, never in the composite. Quote with signal_target_transform or not at all. Needs a spread (knn1 / avg-arcsinh absent). Not comparable to NB NLL. Count-space NLL and p-value-space NLL never share a table.

count/crps.question: If each bin is a negative-binomial forecast of raw counts, how far is that whole distribution from the held-out count?
count/crps.estimator_notes: Default: closed-form CRPS = E|X − y| − ½ E|X − X′| (metrics.py::nb_crps), p = n / (n + μ) clipped to [10⁻⁹, 1 − 10⁻⁹], y ← max(y, 0). For n ≤ 10⁴: Pfaff-transformed ₂F₁ Gini term; result clamped max(·, 0). For n > 10⁴: Poisson-limit branch with sd ratio r = √(1 + μ/n). Track mean then macro mean. Opt-in --crps-approx K: fair sampled CRPS (nb_crps_sampled), k = K (full-genome baselines planned k=100, seed 0), gamma–Poisson draws, Ferro 2008 denominator k(k−1), no clamp at 0. Provenance then carries crps_estimator=fair_sampled, crps_k, crps_seed. Stamped chromosome-21 baselines: closed form at producer floor n=10⁴, not the pre-registered 10⁶. Computed from metrics.py::nb_crps and distributional.py::nb_suite.
count/crps.read_rules: Lower is better; ranked; floor ±0.09 (frozen pre-CANDII target-clustered; not a full-genome cross-method remeasure). Always quote crps_oracle_scaled and scale_error. If sampled, also quote k and seed. CANDI self-arrows use the 0.1195 seed-alone bar, not this floor. Count and p-value CRPS never share a column.

count/crps_oracle_scaled.question: After giving the forecast a free per-assay multiplicative rescale of the mean, how good is the distribution (capability)?
count/crps_oracle_scaled.estimator_notes: c* = arg min_c CRPS(NB(n, μ · 2^c), y) on grid c ∈ [−6, 6] step 0.25 then refine ±0.25 at 0.01 (distributional.py::oracle_scale). Grid search may subsample fit_budget=20,000 positions (seed=0); reported CRPS is on the full track at chosen c*. Dispersion n is not rescaled for this key. Same estimator as crps (closed form or sampled with shared seed). In-sample oracle: scale_error may be slightly negative. Computed from distributional.py::oracle_scale / nb_suite.
count/crps_oracle_scaled.read_rules: Lower is better; companion. Never quote without raw crps and scale_error. Not a cross-method rank column by itself.

count/scale_error.question: How much of the count CRPS would one per-assay mean rescale remove?
count/scale_error.estimator_notes: scale_error = crps − crps_oracle_scaled (distributional.py::nb_suite). Same estimator on both terms (common random numbers if sampled).
count/scale_error.read_rules: Lower is better (can be slightly negative); companion. Quote the triple or none.

count/nb_nll.question: What mean per-bin negative-binomial NLL does the count head assign to held-out raw counts?
count/nb_nll.estimator_notes: Training twin (distributional.py::nb_nll): p = n / (n + μ), probs = clip(1 − p, [10⁻⁶, 1 − 10⁻⁶]), total = max(n, 10⁻⁶), k = max(counts, 0), NLL = −mean[total log(1 − probs) + k log(probs) − log Γ(total + k) + log Γ(1 + k) + log Γ(total)]. Mean over all eval bins of the track (the imp population, not a training mask). Computed from distributional.py::nb_nll / harness.py::loss_block.
count/nb_nll.read_rules: Lower is better; per_family; never in the composite; never ranked against Gaussian NLL. Sampled CRPS does not change NLL. Count-space NLL and p-value-space NLL never share a table.

diagnostics/covuse.question: Does scrambling one told covariate make the count-head CRPS worse than the true prompt?
diagnostics/covuse.estimator_notes: Per covariate k, L_obs = mean CRPS_NB(predict(cov)). For R = 200 resamples (default, seed 0): marginal and conditional nulls; p = (1 + #{L_r ≤ L_obs}) / (R + 1); uses_covariate = 1[p_marginal < 0.05]. within_batch_d_crps must be exactly 0 (covariate.py::covuse). Board scalar: flatten_c_block has no headline for nested covuse — omitted unless already a finite scalar. Computed from covariate.py::covuse.
diagnostics/covuse.read_rules: Registry direction is higher, but no panel aggregate is defined in code. CANDI-lineage only; empty for every stamped row; never invent for rivals.

diagnostics/covshare.question: Of the variance in predicted level, what share does each covariate own (Shapley, not Sobol)?
diagnostics/covshare.estimator_notes: Shapley effects on V(S) = Var(E[f | X_S]) with inner-sample bias correction, both variances ddof=1, n_outer=64, n_inner=8, seed 0, f = level (covariate.py::covshare). Four covariates → 16 subsets exact. Shares sum to 1 when total > 10⁻¹². Board scalar: none (per-covariate dict omitted by flatten).
diagnostics/covshare.read_rules: No direction on the registry; no board number today; CANDI-only. Never invent for rivals.

diagnostics/depthdir.question: As told depth is stepped down the DSF ladder, does predicted level fall at every step?
diagnostics/depthdir.estimator_notes: Ladder offsets (0, −1, −2, −3) log2 (covariate.py::depthdir). monotone_frac = mean(Δlevel ≤ 0) over adjacent steps × units. Headline on the board = monotone_frac.
diagnostics/depthdir.read_rules: Higher is better; diagnostic; CANDI-only; not in the composite. Never invent for rivals.

diagnostics/depthcounterfact.question: Told a false depth, does the count forecast whose told depth matches the real downsampled track win?
diagnostics/depthcounterfact.estimator_notes: One foreground: top 2% (min 5) of the deepest truth, jitter seed 0, optional truth ≥ 1 purity (covariate.py::depthcounterfact). For each true DSF level, argmin CRPS over told depths. Board headline = frac_min_at_true. constant_answer_value = 1 / n_levels (0.25 on a four-level ladder).
diagnostics/depthcounterfact.read_rules: Higher is better; quote with the 0.25 floor and no 0.73 ceiling. 0.25 is “always answer full depth”, not chance. CANDI-only.

diagnostics/covspec.question: When each covariate is scrambled, does each aspect of the NB profile move mainly under one covariate?
diagnostics/covspec.estimator_notes: Aspects = level, shape, dispersion, tail (aspects_of). Matrix entry = mean |Δaspect| / std(base aspect) under marginal resample. Per aspect, gap = (m_1 − m_2) / m_1. Board headline = mean_gap (covariate.py::covspec). Construction is local (EVAL_PLAN D11), not a standard MIG of latents.
diagnostics/covspec.read_rules: Higher is better; diagnostic; CANDI-only; not in the composite.

diagnostics/depthblind.question: Is the encoder latent invariant to input depth (DSF batch), by kBET / iLISI / batch ASW?
diagnostics/depthblind.estimator_notes: depthblind returns kBET rejection rate (k=20, α=0.05, n_test=200, seed 0), iLISI (k capped), batch_asw = mean(1 − |s|), plus biokeep fields (covariate.py::depthblind). Board: flatten_c_block omits depthblind — no single headline. Site cannot show a number until a headline is chosen. Computed from covariate.py::depthblind / kBET.
diagnostics/depthblind.read_rules: Higher better on the registry, but no scalar is extracted. Never quote without biokeep (D13). CANDI-only.

diagnostics/biokeep.question: Did the latent stay invariant because it still separates regions, or because it collapsed?
diagnostics/biokeep.estimator_notes: Mean silhouette over bio_label (region) (covariate.py::biokeep). Board headline from depthblind_biokeep.bio_silhouette (flatten_c_block).
diagnostics/biokeep.read_rules: Higher is better; companion of depthblind; never render depth-blind without this; CANDI-only.
